locator: I q.2 a.3 co., tertia via: quod possibile est non esse, quandoque non est
interpretation: Reading B, plenitude: the sentence is an instance of the Aristotelian principle that what is possible is at some time realized in infinite time (De caelo I.12, not pinned), here applied over an infinite past and to any possible condition, including 'nothing is'. Stronger than reading A (plenitudeYieldsDistributive). The infinite past is not asserted in the text and is a separate premise (STMT-PAST-IS-INFINITE).
